description.narrative: As a result of institutionalizing and strengthening career guidance for vulnerable host communities and Syrian refugees in the last biennium and strengthened by the ILO in this biennium, the government promoted flexible career guidance resulting into guiding 4,905 job seekers (3941 Jordanians and 964 Syrians), including 1,757 females to help them identify skills needs and support their entry to the labour market. Via the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the Agriculture National Sector Skills Council and the Jordan Agricultural Engineering Association in identifying the occupations in the agriculture sector that require mapping. Based on the agreed occupational map and priority occupations, the ILO will supported the Agriculture National Sectoral Skills Councils in developing four occupational standards and Technical and Vocational Education and Training curricula.

description.narrative: In 2022-23, the National Sectoral Skills Council institutionalized the skill needs assessment and identified the market relevant occupations for Work-Based Learning programme in cooperation with Technical and Vocational Skills Development Council. The report of this assessment is being finalised to be over by September 2023. In September 2023, the Agriculture National Sector Skills Council, in consultations with employers and private sector, developed an “Occupational Map” for the agriculture sector. Via the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the the National Sectoral Skills Council and Technical and Vocational Skills Development Council for skills needs assessment in collaboraiton with the National Sectoral Skills Council , chambers of industries and employers' associations in defining the hard to fill occupations, skills in demand, skills gaps and shortage. The ILO also supported Technical and Vocational Skills Development Council and five selected sector skills councils to identify the skills needs and prioritize the most needed occupations in these sectors and provided capacity building support to the National Sectoral Skills Council , and particulalry for the Agriculture sector skills council in improving visibility and strengthen their capacity to be enggaed in occupational standard development and skills delivery.

description.narrative: In 2022-23, the government of Jordan endorsed the Mehnati portal which is an Employability Readiness Portal to achieve fair and equal employment for youth via the delivery of guidance, access to training & matching for platform jobs & gig opportunities. It is a result of a close collaboration between two entities including ILO and the Ministry of Labour. With the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Labour in developing this job ready portal -Mehanati' to support youth in assessing their job readiness, identify trianing opportunities and opt for online skills trianing.

description.narrative: In July 2023, the Technical and Vocation Skills Development Commission approved a national framework and implementation guide for the Recognition of Prior Learning in Jordan, after extensive consultations with the relevant stakeholders including the National Sector Skills Councils, chambers of commerce and industry, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training providers. The Framework applies equally to Jordanians, migrants and refugees. Via the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the Technical and Vocation Skills Development Commission in the development of the draft RPL framework and operational guide via discussions with the Technical and Vocation Skills Development Commission, National Sectoral Skills Councils, chambers, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training providers and then integrated their inputsin the final draft. With the support of the ILO, the Technical and Vocation Skills Development Commission and the National Sectoral Skills Councils will be rolling out the RPL framework and implementation guide to recognise the skills and experiences of 1,000 workers including Jordanians and Syrian refugees in sectors including tourism, agriculture, construction, logistics, chemicals, and garment.

description.narrative: In September 2022, a unified standard system for developing national occupational standards was adopted by the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission and implemented. Furthermore, in February 2023, the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission endorsed the guidelines for the accreditation of work-based learning programmes, which is the first guidelines on work-based learning in Jordan. The Standard Classification of Occupations 2004 and 2021 versions were mapped by the Ministry of Labour and then endorsed and implemented in December 2023. With the support from the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO supported the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission in developing an operational manual for the standard processes and template for the new system of National Occupational Standards in consultations with the National Sectoral Skills Councils, chambers, and related providers. In December 2023, the ILO supported the the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission in training and certifying national facilitators to develop the National Occupational Standards based on the new system. Furthermore, the ILO supported the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission in reviewing seven Technical and Vocational Education and Training legislations in consultations with the National Sectoral Skills Councils and Technical and Vocational Education and Training providers. As a result, the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission developed a draft guideline for the work-based learning as first guidelines on work-based learning in Jordan. The guidelines were revised by the ILO, providing extensive inputs and changes to align guidelines with ILO principles on work-based learning and apprenticeship. Finally, the ILO supported the MoL in mapping the different versions of the the Jordan Standard Classification of Occupations versions.

description.narrative: The Technical and Vocational Skills Decelopement Commission suopprted 371job seekers from Amman, Irbid, Mafraq, and Zarqa governorates to complete their work-based learning programs in market relevant occupations in sectors such as green jobs, agro-food, digital, tourism, crafts and related trades, thereby implementing the outcome of the strategy and its action plan.
